chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If you are in a land of fear, and you fear a thief or a predatory beast, then pray (Salat) upon your animal.'
ai.seo_question: How does one perform prayer while riding an animal during times of fear?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the flexibility of Salat al-Khawf, specifically permitting prayer while mounted on a beast to maintain vigilance against thieves or wild beasts. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease (rukhas) in times of danger, where the primary concern is preserving life and awareness while fulfilling the obligation of prayer.
